title: Mexico introduces a one-peso-per-litre tax on sugar-sweetened drinks
context: Mexico had high consumption of sugary drinks and rising obesity.
decision_made: Apply an excise tax of about 1 peso per litre from January 2014.
action_taken: Researchers tracked store purchase data for 2012 to 2015.
observed_outcome: Prices rose by about the tax amount. Purchases of taxed drinks fell by about 5.5 percent in 2014 and 9.7 percent in 2015, with the biggest drops among lowest-income households, while purchases of untaxed drinks rose slightly.
lessons: A tax passed fully into prices can reduce purchases, especially among lower-income households.
limitations: Estimates use store purchase data and a counterfactual model, and the 2014 figure was revised from 6 percent to 5.5 percent in a later paper. Health outcomes were not measured here.

claims.claim_text: Mexico introduced an excise tax on sugar-sweetened beverages of about one peso per litre in 2014.
A follow-up study found taxed beverage purchases fell 5.5 percent in 2014 and 9.7 percent in 2015.
